summary: In the early 1930s the city was still assembling this district out of private lots. It exchanged land with Louis Depaoli to push Theresa Street through to Cayuga Avenue, took a deed from Cora Plate for the ground Alemany Boulevard needed, and in 1933 declared Cayuga Avenue and Shakespeare Street to be open public streets for the first time. Other streets went the other way in the same years: parts of Liebig Street and Regent Street were closed and abandoned.

summary_sources.t: Authorizing the exchange of certain lands with Louis Depaoli, setting aside $8,500 out of County Road Fund, and authorizing its payment to Louis Depaoli, said lands being required for the extension of Theresa street between Alemany boulevard and Cayuga avenue.
Approved July 7, 1933, be and is hereby approved, and the parcels shown hatched thereon be and are hereby declared to be an open public street to be known as Shakespeare street.

Approved September 1, 1933, be and is hereby approved, and the parcels numbers 1 to 4, both inclusive, shown hatched thereon be and are hereby declared to be an open public street to be known as Cayuga avenue.
The City and County of San Francisco accept a deed from Cora E. Plate to a portion of Lot 9, Assessor's Block 7156, San Francisco, required for Alemany boulevard.
